The robot playground demo can only be tried by cloning the repository and running `npm run example`. There is no hosted version, so someone evaluating three-webmcp cannot open it from the README.

## Expected outcome

- GitHub Pages is enabled for the repository with GitHub Actions as the source.
- The example build (`npm run example:build`) is deployed to GitHub Pages automatically when `main` is updated, using GitHub Actions.
- The robot playground works at https://takahirox.github.io/three-webmcp/, including the locally bundled robot model and its attribution/license files.
- The README links to the hosted demo, and still explains that a WebMCP-enabled browser and a connected agent are needed to control it with an AI.
- Existing local development (`npm run example`) keeps working.

## Context

- The cube example is being removed in #11; only the robot playground needs to be published.
- The example build already exists: `npm run example:build` outputs `example-dist/`.
- The site is served under the `/three-webmcp/` path, not the domain root.

outputs.message:
Issue #10 is closed. GitHub closed it automatically when PR #12 was merged (merge commit bf1fca2056b1ec36b8867d3b8132abfff5525f8f), so I didn't need to close it myself. I posted a comment on the issue with the outcome: https://github.com/takahirox/three-webmcp/issues/10#issuecomment-5883904808

The site isn't live yet. The first "Deploy demo to GitHub Pages" run (https://github.com/takahirox/three-webmcp/actions/runs/36523727681) and the CI run were both still queued when I checked. https://takahirox.github.io/three-webmcp/ returns 404 for now because nothing has been deployed. Someone should confirm that run succeeds and the page then loads.

The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need to be authorized in claude.ai connector settings before they can be used. This step didn't need them.
